r0040: 3.  Everyone charged with a criminal offence has the following minimum rights:
r0042: b)  to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence;
r0043: c)  to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing or, if he has not sufficient means to pay for legal assistance, to be given it free when the interests of justice so require;
r0046: 14.  The Government asked the Court to dismiss the complaint concerning the composition of the State Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l'Etat*) for failure to comply with the six-month time-limit laid down in Article 35 of the Convention. They submitted that the final domestic decision in respect of the complaint concerning the lack of independence and impartiality of the State Security Court was the one delivered by that court itself. In that connection, they argued that neither the State Security Court nor the Court of Cassation (*Cour de cassation*) had been empowered to rule on that complaint, since the composition of the State Security Courts had been laid down, at the material time, by domestic legislation. They concluded that the applicant should have lodged his application within six months of the time when he had become aware of the ineffectiveness of the domestic remedies, that is, from 29 December 1997, the date of the State Security Court's judgment. They pointed out, however, that the application had been lodged on 17 September 1999.
r0047: 15.  The Court reiterates that it dismissed a similar objection in Özdemir v. Turkey (judgment cited above, § 26). It sees no reason to depart from that conclusion and therefore dismisses the Government's objection.
r0048: 16.  The Court considers, in the light of the criteria established in its case-law (see, in particular, Çiraklar v. Turkey, judgment of 28 October 1998, Reports of Judgments and Decisions 1998-VII) and having regard to all the evidence before it, that these complaints require an examination on the merits. It further notes that they are not inadmissible on any other grounds.
